target: uncommitted tracked working diff plus seven new executable files
method: single-reviewer sequential dimension passes, followed by source reread and refute-first reproductions; no subagents

findings.title: Do not infer that an unpaid residual is spurious from its size alone
findings.reach: canonical Portfolio adapter; every strategy; also future cash continuation
findings.actual: H2 modeled, a=0, b=97, cash=255, net=158; H1 had a=2^-40 and H2 payment/interest for a were both zero
findings.expected: H0/H1 remain available; H2 onward unavailable cent-tolerance, since genuine entered inventory disappeared without repayment
findings.refutation: Confirmed after rereading allocation and adapter. All input amounts are exactly representable binary rationals, APR is zero, and (256+2^-40)-256 is exact. The previous-operation epsilon bound cannot establish that this residual was a rounding artifact. The effect is sub-cent, not a claimed cents-level financial loss. No arbitrary-precision production math or lender posting is required to recognize the unsupported clearance.

findings.title: Guard required rows before dereferencing month
findings.reach: generic trace reducer malformed-input boundary; not reproduced via current canonical engine output
findings.actual: Valid H1 works; H2 with rows=[validRow,null] throws TypeError reading month
findings.expected: H2 unavailable invalid-trace with coveredThroughMonth=1; same treatment for a required sparse row
findings.refutation: Confirmed. The guard only establishes that rows is an array, not that every element is a position. TypeScript does not validate the runtime trace, and the explicitly promised malformed-trace fail-closed boundary already validates other row fields. This is not a demonstrated crash in the current Portfolio UI.

findings.title: Retain interest residuals until signed conservation has completed
findings.reach: generic trace reducer finite high-magnitude precision contract; no canonical Portfolio policy reproduction claimed
findings.actual: H2 unavailable inconsistent-trace, coverage=1, after cumulative interest 1e16+1 was rounded to 1e16
findings.expected: H2 modeled net=-1; all raw conservation terms sum exactly to zero
findings.refutation: Confirmed. All inputs and the final net -1 are finite exactly represented integers. The existing partial-sum helper returns raw conservation residual 0; only pre-collapsing interest causes residual -1 and the rejection. Rounded interestThroughMonth is an acceptable diagnostic, but should not be fed back into the validation oracle. This finding requests residual preservation, not arbitrary-precision lender posting.

coverageGapsNotFindings: The browser helper changes horizon but never changes selected strategy; seeded reference columns do not prove current-selection UI updates.
New browser cases are guest-only and always provide a book; they do not assert the comparison draft and result after owner changes or absent-book hydration.
The seven unchanged hook contracts exercise actual React reconciliation with null host surfaces and mocked storage, not the new comparison view, browser, or physical storage.

The seeded reference suite has a separate direct ledger and independent row accounting, but much of Velocity's expected inventory is still read from production rows. Counts are not independent policy completeness.

Geometry controls prove zero-opacity, clipping, and empty-value rejection when run; the source does not establish absence of all occlusion, low-opacity, color/contrast, label-overlap, or native text-scaling failures.
strengths: Same canonical decoded book and explicit decimal APR are used for all three policies.
Prepared traces are private to each captured book and atMonth returns fresh maps and payoff metadata.
Current selected policy is used for signed deltas, and unavailable references do not fabricate zero deltas.
Existing native storageScope keys and absent-book conditional remain in place; no new persistence path or cross-owner cache.
The four browser-oracle negative controls preserve original text-node identity and restore styles.
